I am 68 years old and have farmed these fields in Quzhou County my whole life. I only finished primary school, but I know this soil and climate better than any book. I manage about 14 mu of flat, good-quality land. At my age, I do not want to take risks with labor-intensive crops like cotton or vegetables, and I cannot do heavy hand-picking anymore. My son helps me with the machines, so I stick to the safe, mechanized winter wheat–summer maize rotation that everyone in our village grows. The winter wheat went into the ground last October and is greening up now. I will irrigate it four times—especially at jointing and grain filling—and apply compound fertilizer as a topdressing. I will also spray for insects, weeds, and disease about four times. After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize directly into the stubble without ploughing, which saves diesel and labor. The maize needs two irrigations, three pesticide sprays, and one basal fertilizer application. I use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because they give steady, good yields on my land.
